papers.title: From patient cells to patient therapy: Twenty years of iPSC-based translation in neurodegenerative disease
papers.summary: Cha and Kim review two decades of iPSC-based translation in neurodegenerative disease, highlighting disease-specific therapeutic logic and the emerging importance of transplantation biology. They propose a phase-resolved framework for the post-transplant “biological black box” linking graft survival, maturation, host interactions, and long-term therapeutic outcome.

papers.title: Multi-omics-driven personalized management of advanced HCC
papers.summary: Sheng et al. integrate spatial multi-omics, functional models, and clinical validation to show that fibrotic stroma suppresses epithelial cGAS-STING signaling and T cell recruitment in HCC. Their GCSS model links tumor architecture to response prediction for TACE plus immune checkpoint blockade.

papers.title: Enhanced liver regeneration via targeted mRNA delivery for partial in vivo reprogramming
papers.summary: Jo et al. show that transient OSKM induction generates two distinct liver progenitor-like cell populations with limited immune activation. Liver-targeted OSKM mRNA-LNPs induce hepatocyte dedifferentiation and enhance regeneration after acetaminophen-induced liver injury, supporting transient hepatic reprogramming as a strategy for inducing regenerative plasticity with therapeutic potential for acute injury.

papers.title: In vivo-edited CCR7+IL-7+ DCs reverse T cell exhaustion by promoting T memory stem cell differentiation
papers.summary: Fu and Ma et al. develop DVH to edit DCs into CCR7+IL-7+ DCs, which target the T-zone within TDLNs and secrete IL-7 to promote Tscm differentiation. The Tscms can self-renew and generate effector T cells under antigen stimulation continuously, thereby killing tumor cells and reducing T cell exhaustion at the source.

papers.title: EZH2-dependent phenotypic plasticity reveals TTP-associated and mTORC1 therapeutic vulnerabilities in lethal prostate cancer
papers.summary: German et al. use integrated multi-omics analysis to identify EZH2 as a central regulator of prostate cancer phenotypic plasticity. The study reveals TTP-associated pathways and adaptive PI3K/mTORC1 as mediators of response to EZH2 inhibition and demonstrates that co-targeting EZH2 and PI3K/mTORC1 is an effective strategy in aggressive prostate cancer models.

papers.title: Reversal of the neutrophil barrier for potentiating immune-engineered bacteria therapy in pancreatic cancer
papers.summary: Guan et al. develop an IAA-assisted engineered bacterial therapy for pancreatic cancer. IAA suppresses neutrophil recruitment and synergizes with gemcitabine to eliminate neutrophils, boosting bacterial colonization and antitumor immune efficacy.

papers.title: A multi-omics analysis of advanced triple-negative breast cancer identifies predictors to chemo-immunotherapy and on-treatment dynamics
papers.summary: Van Renne, Agostinetto, et al. perform a multi-omics characterization of advanced TNBC to identify response predictors and treatment-induced dynamics during chemo-ICI. Poor outcomes are associated with fibrovascular and myeloid remodeling, highlighting coordinated resistance mechanisms, actionable therapeutic targets, and the value of microenvironment-based stratification for future ICI-based trials.

papers.title: Potently neutralizing and protective human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein trimer
papers.summary: Handal et al. isolate a panel of naturally occurring human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein that potently neutralize in vitro and inhibit viral replication in vivo, demonstrating strong clinical potential. Two antibodies bind distinct portions of the F protein simultaneously with epitopes spanning across multiple F protomers.

papers.title: Structural basis for broad orthopoxvirus neutralization by two antibodies targeting distinct L1R epitopes
papers.summary: Chen et al. identify two neutralizing antibodies, G4 and B9, targeting distinct epitopes on the mpox virus M1R protein (an L1R homolog). Despite targeting a conventional epitope, G4 overcomes Asp35-associated neutralization escape. Both antibodies protect against multiple orthopoxviruses in vitro and in vivo, supporting their potential as broad-spectrum antiviral candidates.

papers.title: Potentiating immunotherapy in “immune-cold” solid tumors through orchestrating T cell immunity via tumor-specific genetic engineering
papers.summary: (Cell Reports Medicine 6, 102510; December 16, 2025)

papers.title: Human iPSC models of myocardial infarction: From injury to repair and therapeutic discovery
papers.summary: Johnson et al. review how human induced pluripotent stem cells can model key stages of myocardial infarction, focusing on cell types involved across acute injury, repair, and remodeling. They examine current model strengths and limitations and discuss emerging applications in therapeutic discovery, patient-specific modeling, and regenerative cardiac repair.

papers.title: Punicalin targets RSV glycoprotein and fusion protein at non-overlapping sites to prevent viral escape
papers.summary: Xiong et al. identify that punicalin broadly inhibits respiratory syncytial virus subtypes and clinical isolates by targeting the viral G and F proteins at sites outside known resistance hotspots. It retains potent activity against drug-resistant virus and, when delivered by nebulization, reduces pulmonary viral burden and inflammation in infected mice.

papers.title: Multipronged enhancement of CART cell activity against ROR1 neoantigen by inhibition of H3K27 methyltransferase EZH2
papers.summary: Wang et al. report that inhibition of EZH2 and, to lesser degree, other epigenetic modifiers promotes expression of ROR1 neoantigen on malignant cells. CART cells targeting ROR1 are able to detect the neoantigen at very low concentration and, in combination with EZH2 inhibition, highly effectively eliminate the ROR1-expressing cells.

papers.title: iPSC-derived retinal organoids: Biological insights and progress toward photoreceptor replacement therapy
papers.summary: Mandai et al. review iPSC-derived photoreceptor replacement therapy, contrasting cone precursor and retinal organoid transplantations. They highlight host-dependent cone integration, gene-edited organoids for enhanced integration, and synaptic rewiring in the adult primate retina, providing a framework to restore vision in patients with untreatable retinal degenerations.

papers.title: Functional O-specific polysaccharide-specific antibody responses in young children following Shigella infection in Bangladesh
papers.summary: Bernshtein et al. show that functional antibodies correlate with milder shigellosis at any age, yet only individuals over 5 years of age mount lasting responses to the surface O-specific polysaccharide that drives Shigella uptake by phagocytes and triggers IL-1β and IL-18 release.

papers.title: Genome-wide cell-free DNA methylation profiling via TAPS for moyamoya disease diagnosis and postoperative collateral formation prediction
papers.summary: Chen et al. apply multimodal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) profiling via TET-assisted pyridine borane sequencing to moyamoya disease. They identify cfDNA methylation signatures that distinguish moyamoya disease from atherosclerotic cerebrovascular disease and predict postoperative collateral formation, supporting minimally invasive diagnosis and preoperative assessment of moyamoya disease.

papers.title: Combining pro-resolving therapy with cyclosporine A restores immune homeostasis and reduces toxicity in autoimmune bone marrow failure
papers.summary: Grazda et al. show that defective inflammation resolution persists in autoimmune bone marrow failure, despite standard-of-care cyclosporine A therapy. Combining resolvin E1 with cyclosporine A restores immune homeostasis while reducing toxicity.

papers.title: A blood-based metabolic signature for earlier detection of lung cancer
papers.summary: Irajizad et al. report a blood-based metabolite panel for earlier detection of lung cancer. The metabolite panel complements clinical risk models for lung cancer incidence and mortality. The panel provides a means for identifying ever-smoker individuals at elevated 1-year risk of lung cancer who would benefit from lung cancer screening.

papers.title: Therapeutic oligonucleotides as genetic medicines: The current state and future perspective
papers.summary: Godinho et al. provide an overview of nucleic acid therapies, a new class of programmable drugs that enable disease-modifying treatments by acting at the gene transcript level. The authors summarize key advances in chemistry and delivery and offer a perspective on the advances expected in the near future.

papers.title: Targeting RPL4 improves the therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1 blockade in liver fibrosis
papers.summary: Zhang et al. identify a key profibrotic function of FBXL6 in hepatic stellate cells through activation of the RPL4-YY1-PD-L1-PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis. Targeting RPL4 in combination with PD-L1 blockade achieves near-complete resolution of liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Early diagnosis and molecular classification of gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis by deep learning-driven single-cell lipidomics
papers.summary: Pan et al. combine single-cell lipidomics and graph deep learning to identify occult peritoneal metastasis in gastric cancer. The label-free platform detects rare free cancer cells, supports molecular stratification, and delivers patient-level diagnostic results within 30 min.

papers.title: Characterization of circulating neoantigen-specific T cell responses and public T cell receptors shaping immune memory in Lynch syndrome carriers
papers.summary: Duzagac et al. show that circulating tissue-surveillance neoantigen-specific T cells are detectable in Lynch syndrome carriers, even before cancer onset. Their metabolic states differ by disease stage, separating cancer-free carriers from survivors. Public TCRs spanning blood and tumor tissue open a non-invasive window for immunoprevention in mismatch repair-deficient cancers.

papers.title: Class visualizations and activation atlases for computational pathology
papers.summary: Gustav et al. introduce a concept-level explainability framework that exposes the morphology encoded by a pathology foundation model. The approach reveals prototypical histopathological features and maps the organization and overlap of tissue and cancer concepts, demonstrating that internal model representations reflect both task complexity and pathologist ambiguity.

papers.title: Proteogenomic analysis of pediatric and AYA high-grade glioma reveals age-dependent biology, female-male differences, and kinase targets
papers.summary: Tignor et al. perform a comprehensive proteogenomic analysis of pediatric and AYA high-grade gliomas and identify age- and sex-dependent biology, candidate kinase targets, and proteins and immune signatures associated with poor survival outcomes.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal a recurrent multicellular niche at the tumor-stroma interface in multidrug resistance
papers.summary: Shen et al. map the evolutionary trajectory of multi-drug resistance (MDR) across cancers, revealing a biophysical spatial nexus formed by specific fibroblasts, macrophages, and tumor cells. They demonstrate that dismantling this multicellular barrier-like niche with an FAP/TREM2 bispecific antibody safely restores therapeutic sensitivity, highlighting a targeted strategy to resensitize MDR.

papers.title: Allosteric modulation of YTHDFs by ellagic acid suppresses triple-negative breast cancer via non-canonical activation of the HIF-1α pathway
papers.summary: Zhou et al. identify ellagic acid (EA) as an allosteric inhibitor of YTHDF proteins that binds to a conserved site shared across YTHDF family members. By disrupting YTHDF2-mediated RNA decay, EA stabilizes PFKFB4 mRNA to prevent HIF-1α degradation and upregulates BNIP3 expression, thereby driving triple-negative breast cancer cell death.

papers.title: Single-cell tracking reveals tumor-reactive T cell plasticity during melanoma TIL therapy
papers.summary: Sandholzer et al. track tumor-reactive T cells across TIL therapy in metastatic melanoma using single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing. They show how ex vivo expansion reshapes CD8+ and CD4+ T cell states and links type 17 T cell co-transfer and regulatory T cell expansion to treatment resistance.

papers.title: First-line fecal microbiota transplantation for the management of immune checkpoint inhibitor-mediated diarrhea and colitis
papers.summary: Wang et al. report the efficacy of a preliminary cohort of patients who receive first-line fecal microbiota transplantation for the management of immune-mediated diarrhea and colitis with multi-omics characterization. Response is seen in 10 out of 13 patients, with an increase in alpha-diversity in a majority of patients who respond.

papers.title: Neutrophil elastase-mediated myoepithelial loss is a therapeutic vulnerability in ductal carcinoma in situ progression
papers.summary: Transition from ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) to invasive breast cancer remains a key step in disease progression that is poorly understood. Taifour et al. show that neutrophil elastase disrupts the myoepithelial barrier to promote invasive progression, identifying neutrophil elastase as a potential therapeutic target for high-risk DCIS.

papers.title: Bi-hourly plasma proteomics during the first 48 h of life in an African cohort reveals distinct periods and sex-dependent immune development
papers.summary: Bennike et al. profile plasma proteins and cytokines/chemokines in 679 healthy newborns through mass spectrometry and immunoassays to characterize immune adaptation during the 48 h immediately after birth at bi-hourly resolution. They reveal non-linear trajectories and sex-specific differences especially during day-of-life one, providing a molecular framework for early-life immune development.

papers.title: Targeted insertion of an optimized donor DNA is effective in a humanized mouse model of dominant retinitis pigmentosa
papers.summary: Esposito et al. develop a donor-optimized, mutation-agnostic AAV-HITI strategy for dominant rhodopsin-associated retinitis pigmentosa that simultaneously disrupts the mutant RHO P23H allele and restores rhodopsin expression through targeted integration at the human RHO locus, improving retinal structure, function, and vision in a semi-humanized mouse disease model, up to one year.

papers.title: L013 promotes NRF2 degradation in NRFA-subtype esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
papers.summary: Yu et al. identify L013 as an NRF2-targeting agent that reduces NRF2 via UPS-associated degradation and A51-mediated suppression. L013 inhibits tumor growth in preclinical models, revealing therapeutic potential for NRFA-subtype ESCC.

papers.title: Intoxication and other subjective effects of preanesthetic opioids in surgical patients: A randomized controlled trial
papers.summary: Karlsen et al. show that patients experience marked undesirable effects but minimal desirable effects after preoperative intravenous opioids.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data
papers.summary: Martínez-Mateu et al. develop a computational framework that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomes from patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize combination therapies. They identify anti-TNF plus anti-IL-6R as complementary in rheumatoid arthritis, localize the effect to CD14+ monocytes, and validate the combination in mice, nominating candidates for clinical testing.

papers.title: A stem-like chromatin program in small-cell lung cancer is associated with poor outcomes after chemoimmunotherapy
papers.summary: Kumar et al. use ATAC-seq and transcriptomic analyses to define recurrent chromatin programs in small-cell lung cancer. A stem-like program is associated with metabolic adaptation, reduced immune signaling, and inferior outcomes after chemoimmunotherapy, supporting further development of chromatin-informed biomarkers and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Dendritic cell centric nanoengineering couples antigen acquisition and STING activation for cancer immunotherapy
papers.summary: Xiang et al. develop a dendritic-cell-directed, dual pH-gated nanomedicine that couples CD47-SIRPα relief at the tumor-dendritic cell interface with intracellular STING activation after uptake. This strategy enhances antigen acquisition and T cell cross-priming, suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, and supports the translation of STING immunotherapy.

papers.title: Transforming large language models into medical specialists via knowledge injection
papers.summary: Kim et al. review knowledge-injection strategies transforming general-purpose large language models into medical specialists—internalizing medical knowledge, aligning behavior with clinical norms, and grounding outputs in real-time evidence—plus multimodal integration and agentic AI, charting a roadmap toward safe, trustworthy clinical AI.

papers.title: This week in charts: Kodiak’s big comeback and Hengrui’s dealmaking
papers.summary: The latest installment in BioPharma Dive’s data visualization series features a closer look at Kodiak’s stock performance and Hengrui's ties with U.S. and European drugmakers.

papers.title: Novartis wagers almost $8B on a Chinese biotech’s RNA drugs
papers.summary: In exchange for a $575 million payment up front, Abogen Biosciences will furnish Novartis with access to its RNA technology, including an option to license its lead program ABO-2203.

papers.title: 3 takeaways from a European obesity scientific meeting
papers.summary: Eli Lilly impressed with its amylin-Zepbound combination data. Elsewhere, Novo demonstrated continued weight loss following a switch to oral and AbbVie and Boehringer gave glimpses into their contenders.

papers.title: Lilly, Foghorn part ways; Wave’s FDA-approved plans
papers.summary: The pharma giant cut its partnership after a cancer drug disappointed in testing. Elsewhere, Teva and Samsung Bioepis expanded a partnership and space biotech Varda brought in $251 million.

papers.title: Sanofi, Regeneron broaden alliance to find their next Dupixent
papers.summary: The deal carries a $1 billion upfront payment and tasks the two companies to develop long-acting antibody drugs that go after the same targets as their blockbuster anti-inflammation agent.

papers.title: HHS kicks off new programs to speed clinical trials as Chinese competition looms
papers.summary: The department is offering funding to teams with innovative proposals as it considers ending the traditional phased clinical trial system.

papers.title: Pfizer’s eczema drug clears skin in mid-stage trial
papers.summary: Detailed results are competitive with Dupixent and Ebglyss, but the drug lacks differentiation amid an increasingly competitive landscape, one analyst argued.

papers.title: 5 FDA decisions to watch in the fourth quarter of 2026
papers.summary: The next three months will feature anticipated decisions on a new kind of cancer immunotherapy, as well as medicines important to the futures of Roche, GSK and Gilead.

papers.title: Bristol Myers trial revisions shake confidence in new class of fibrosis drugs
papers.summary: A spokesperson confirmed that a “limited number” of liver-related safety events, including a patient death, were observed in testing of Bristol Myers’ admilparant — though it’s unclear whether the drug was to blame.

papers.title: FDA starts review of Roche’s multiple sclerosis pill
papers.summary: The FDA previously hadn’t ever accepted an application of a drug like fenebrutinib in two major forms of MS. But safety questions still hang over Roche’s program.

When Xaira Therapeutics first debuted in 2024 with a gobsmacking $1 billion in funding, a natural expectation would have been for a flurry of further activity to follow. Instead, the buzzy AI biotech went quiet.

Eric Cantor, who represented Virginia in the U.S. House of Representatives for 14 years and served as House majority leader from 2011 to 2014, will step up as PhRMA’s next president and CEO on Nov. 9. Plus, Bayer has a new chief medical officer.

Novartis is paying Abogen Biosciences $575 million upfront for an mRNA-encoded T-cell engager that showed early clinical promise in autoimmune disease. The deal, which includes up to $7.2 billion in milestones, comes weeks after Novartis paused an autoimmune CAR-T program over three deaths.
Adecto Pharmaceuticals’ 12-year story has come to an end as the immunotherapy biotech blamed a “risk-averse funding environment” for shutting up shop.

Abbott is kick-starting the U.S. commercial launch of SimpleScreen CRC, an FDA-approved blood-based colorectal cancer (CRC) screening test for adults age 45 and older who are at average risk for the disease.
As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

The revelation of a patient death in Bristol Myers Squibb’s phase 3 trial of a potential pulmonary fibrosis treatment has raised concerns ahead of the study’s readout, but analysts were quick to dispel worries about broader implications for the drug mechanism involved.
Roche Diagnostics has launched a new in vitro diagnostic test for newborn screening to detect a series of rare disorders.
A more subdued volume of biopharma layoffs continued into the third quarter of 2026, validating predictions that the sector has moved beyond the avalanche of redundancies experienced last year.
Foghorn Therapeutics is laying off 40% of its workforce after a long-running collaboration with Eli Lilly collapsed over disappointing phase 1 data.
When recombinant DNA pioneer Herbert Boyer, Ph.D., first got a call from venture capitalist Robert Swanson about starting a company, the savvy scientist wasn’t sure a meeting would be worth his time.

A phase 3 trial of Boehringer Ingelheim’s survodutide in people with obesity and Type 2 diabetes has met its co-primary endpoints. Yet, with the readout echoing earlier data that underwhelmed analysts, shares in Boehringer’s partner Zealand Pharma fell 12% in early trading in Denmark.
Sanofi is paying Regeneron $1 billion upfront to collaborate on four early-stage immunology programs, teeing the longstanding partners up to try to replicate Dupixent’s success.

Eli Lilly announced its amylin-Zepbound combination eloraTZP resulted in 23.3% weight loss in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight, topping its own triple-G drug candidate retatrutide in that population.

Base editing biotech Beam Therapeutics is suing one of its newest rivals, alleging that the upstart company stole the secrets behind one of its lead programs and used them to craft a competing therapy.
Merck & Co. touted a win for its anti-TL1A antibody in a phase 2b trial in patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa (HS).
The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.
GSK is paying Wave Life Sciences $12 million upfront to take ownership of a hepatic program arising from the companies’ long-running collaboration.
Highlight Therapeutics touted positive topline results in patients with localized high-risk head and neck basal cell carcinoma (BCC).

Connect Biopharma has pointed to phase 2 data for its IL-4/IL-13 blocker as proof that the wannabe Dupixent rival can reduce respiratory attacks—although the study missed a secondary endpoint tied to a breathing test.
The FDA has granted 510(k) clearance to Miami-based VertigoDx for its portable diagnostic system that can evaluate vertigo, including benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPVV).
Zealand Pharma has shared primary endpoint data on Roche-partnered petrelintide, revealing that the middle dose of the amylin analog delivered the highest weight loss—9.8%—at Week 28.
Amgen has shed light on its phase 2 lupus win, revealing that its monoclonal antibody daxdilimab was tied to a 6-point reduction in disease severity at the lower dose.

Eli Lilly has shared detailed data from a phase 3 retatrutide trial, revealing that more than one-third of patients on the top dose of the triple-G drug candidate lost at least 25% of their body weight.
A newly launched $5 million clinical trial program allows clinical trial sponsors to start trials in as little as 45 days in Ontario.

DeepEvidence, a new deep research agent, goes beyond retrieving facts and constructs explicit representations of scientific evidence.

papers.title: Large language models discover complementary heuristics for combinatorial optimization
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01307-8 Huatian Gong and colleagues developed LACE, a large language model-based framework that designs optimization algorithms. It builds a verified problem contract, then evolves a portfolio of complementary heuristics that together solve problems that no single method can handle.

papers.title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01309-6 Alonso-Monsalve et al. demonstrate that self-supervised pretraining helps deep learning models to interpret complex neutrino detector events, improving classification, reconstruction and data efficiency while enabling transfer across different neutrino detector technologies.

papers.title: Regional climate risk assessment from climate models using probabilistic machine learning
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01308-7 A generative AI framework called GenFocal is introduced for climate downscaling, producing realistic fine-scale weather from coarse projections and improving regional risk estimates of compound extremes such as heatwaves and tropical cyclones.

papers.title: Task-structured modularity emerges in artificial networks and aligns with brain architecture
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01306-9 Wu et al. show that neural networks learning multiple tasks organize into specialized modules, particularly under capacity constraints. Incremental multitask learning strengthens this modularity and produces architectures resembling brain networks.

papers.title: Minute-scale training for microrobot navigation
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01305-w A vectorized simulator and structured reward framework enable microrobot navigation policies to be trained within minutes and transferred without retraining across robots and environments.

papers.title: Guiding large language models to predict edit sequences for molecular synthesizability optimization
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01304-x Computational drug design often generates molecules that cannot be synthesized. Li and Lai show how large language models can predict precise structural edits to fix these molecules, outperforming traditional methods and preserving key features.

papers.title: Cybernetics, interoception, and the art of embodiment
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01312-x Living organisms continuously monitor their internal physiological states while interacting with complex environments and adapt their actions in response to changes in these internal signals. New work combines such biological principles with cybernetics, reinforcement learning and neuroscience to develop a framework for autonomous and adaptive artificial embodied agents.

papers.title: FLIGHTED: Inferring fitness landscapes from noisy high-throughput experimental data
papers.summary: Sundar et al. present FLIGHTED, a Bayesian method of accounting for uncertainty in protein fitness measurements by generating probabilistic fitness landscapes from noisy high-throughput experiments. FLIGHTED is applied to selection assays and to a high-throughput base-editing assay, and it improves performance of protein fitness models.

papers.title: Systematic transcriptomic evaluation of blastoid models of early human development
papers.summary: Long et al. integrate single-cell transcriptomes across human embryo development to construct a reference and apply complementary metrics to evaluate four blastoid protocols. The analysis reveals differences in cell identity, developmental timing, and lineage structure, providing a systematic basis for comparing and refining blastoid models.

papers.title: CRISPR-associated enzymes are mislocalized to the cytoplasm in iPSC-derived neurons, resulting in KRAB(KOX1)-specific degradation
papers.summary: CRISPR-based genetic tools face unique challenges in iPSC-derived neurons, including expression stability. Here, Cajka et al. show that SV40 NLS-dependent constructs fail to localize to neuronal nuclei, driving cytoplasmic dCas9-KRAB(KOX1) degradation. Alternative NLSs rescue protein localization and expression, revealing mislocalization as a key factor in CRISPR inefficiencies in postmitotic cells.

papers.title: The drifting biochemical basis of an essential molecular interaction
papers.summary: Phylogenetic and experimental reconstruction of an essential molecular interaction across 460 million years reveals that historical substitutions constantly strengthened or weakened random parts of the interface, gradually reshaping the pattern and biochemical basis of affinity as well as the effects of possible mutations.

papers.title: Plasma proteins are integral to cross-tissue gene regulatory networks implicated in cardiometabolic disorders and coronary artery disease
papers.summary: Bankier et al. perform a parallel multi-omic integrative analysis across multiple tissues, using data from the STARNET study, to show that plasma proteins are integral to cross-tissue gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Proteomic signatures for different GRNs are shown to be associated with cardiometabolic outcomes and risk factors.

papers.title: Sampling protein language models for functional protein design
papers.summary: Darmawan et al. introduce multi-mutant sampling strategies for protein language models that exploit epistatic interactions, together with a holistic in silico evaluation framework scoring relevance, quality, and diversity. Benchmarked across diverse protein fitness landscapes, their designs outperform standard single-mutant approaches, and the work offers practical guidance for protein engineering.

papers.title: Evaluation of anti-tumor drugs by simulating physiological absorption and metabolism with a multi-organoid system
papers.summary: Xiao et al. establish a multi-organoid system that integrates intestinal absorption, liver metabolism, and tumor response. This system captures drug activation and inactivation processes overlooked by tumor-only cultures, thus providing a more physiologically relevant approach for predicting the therapeutic efficacy and toxicity of drugs.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit
papers.summary: Small gene regulatory circuits can encode a surprising diversity of dynamical behaviors. A biophysical model of the AC-DC motif reveals over thirty distinct bifurcation structures and shows how molecular regulatory architecture and binding affinity orderings determine oscillations, hysteresis, and multifunctional responses to a single signal.

papers.title: Heterologous engineering of receptors using OrthoRep (HERO) for directed evolution of GPCRs in yeast

papers.title: An AI-powered cloud biofoundry for autonomous biological research
papers.summary: Autonomous experimentation, where an automated system designs, performs, analyzes, and iteratively improves experiments with minimal human intervention represents a transformative scientific research paradigm. However, it remains hampered by the disconnect between computational design and experimental execution. Here we present iCloudBiofoundry, a cloud-accessible, scalable, and self-evolving platform that bridges this divide. A scientific multi-agent system, iBioGenie, plans research workflows by converting natural language research objectives into testable hypotheses and experimentally grounded protocols using literature, databases, and computational tools. A physical AI layer, BiofoundryAI, translates them into executable workflows that run autonomously on distributed robotic biofoundries, and collects the data for iterative design. papers.title: A Lenalidomide-Inducible Suicide Switch for Gene- and Cell-Based Therapy
papers.summary: Genetically modified immune effector cells, including chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells, have emerged as transformative anti-cancer agents. However, these autonomous, living therapies are limited by difficult-to-control hyperactivation toxicities. To achieve their full potential as therapies for a broader range of diseases, CAR T cells must target novel antigens and integrate further potency enhancements that raise the possibility of novel and intensified toxicities. High performance safety systems are needed to restrain these highly active next-generation gene- and cell-based therapies. Cell therapy suicide switches remain infrequently used, and are currently limited by inaccessible controller drugs, incomplete cell depletion, fitness cost, and immunogenicity. papers.title: Rational mRNA Structure -guided Attenuation Enables Embryo-safe in-ovo NDV Vaccination and Protection
papers.summary: Newcastle disease virus (NDV) continues to cause major economic losses in poultry, driving many recent virulent outbreaks. Maternally derived antibodies (MDA) can interfere with the development of active immunity following vaccination in young chicks. NDV vaccine strains that are safe for day-old chicks are not safe for administration to embryos. Here, we combined a computationally guided attenuation strategy with an in-ovo vaccination and challenge study to develop and evaluate an embryo-safe NDV vaccine candidate. Using a large NDV sequence compendium, we applied a local RNA folding energy based algorithm to identify folding selected clusters within the NDV fusion protein; we introduced targeted synonymous substitutions within the first ~900 nucleotides to modulate local RNA structure while preserving the encoded protein sequence. papers.summary: Genome transplantation is a key technology for synthetic genomics, enabling entire genomes to be transferred into recipient cells. Despite its importance, genome transplantation remains confined to a small number of wall-less Mollicute species and is often characterized by low efficiencies, limiting the development and testing of synthetic genomes. Because genome transplantation relies on the same polyethylene glycol mediated DNA delivery process used for plasmid transformation, improving DNA uptake is an important step toward more efficient transplantation systems. Here, we systematically optimized polyethylene glycol-mediated transformation in Mesoplasma florum, a fast-growing, non-pathogenic Mollicute with a reduced genome that represents an attractive chassis for synthetic genomics. papers.title: From Flocks to Swarms: Rewriting the Rules of Collective Cell Migration
papers.summary: From flocking birds to swarming insects, collective motion enables groups to accomplish tasks beyond the capabilities of individuals. These behaviors emerge from local interactions among group members, but the interaction rules that organize collectives at the cellular scale remain poorly understood, in part because they are difficult to manipulate experimentally. Here we develop a cell-machine interface that enables us to rewrite the rules of collective migration. Cell-cell interaction rules are specified in software and implemented in living cells through real-time computer vision and closed-loop optogenetic control. Using a single engineered cell line, we program cells to self-organize into flocks, to propagate regenerative signal relays that recapitulate the interaction logic of immune-cell swarms, and to collectively navigate guidance cues that individual cells cannot. papers.title: Coupled enzyme discovery, evolution and synthetic yeast chassis adaptation for microbial biopolymer valorisation
papers.summary: The valorisation of biological polymers requires microbial systems that can both access recalcitrant substrates and convert the resulting carbon into useful products. Although microbial genome and metagenome resources provide an expanding reservoir of candidate depolymerizing and modifying enzymes, most discovery workflows remain disconnected from enzyme optimisation and host adaptation. Here we present a coupled sequence-based enzyme discovery, enzyme evolution and synthetic yeast chassis adaptation strategy for microbial biopolymer valorisation. Focusing on laccases for the depolymerisation of lignin as a proof of concept, we combine sequence data mining for enzyme discovery, modular yeast surface display for functional screening, directed evolution for enzyme optimisation and synthetic yeast genome diversification for chassis improvement. papers.title: Multichromatic Dynamic Control of Multi-Membered Microbial Consortia Compositions for Chemical Production
papers.summary: Engineered microbial consortia offer a promising strategy for chemical production by distributing specialized functions among microbial strains, reducing metabolic burden, facilitating modular pathway optimization, reducing toxicity, and increasing strain stability. However, differences in growth rates can destabilize population composition, compromising productivity and limiting their applicability. Here, we developed a multichromatic optogenetic Toxin-Antitoxin (optogeneticTA) platform for dynamic control of Escherichia coli consortia of up to four members using blue, red, and near-infrared light and darkness. By varying light intensities or pulses, we precisely program and dynamically modulate the population composition of two-, three-, and four-membered consortia. papers.title: PRIME: A modular plasmid-based platform for continuous in vivo evolution across bacteria
papers.summary: Directed evolution enables the engineering of proteins with novel or improved functions, yet existing approaches often require extensive manual intervention and are difficult to sustain over long evolutionary trajectories. Here we introduce PRIME (Protein-primed Replication for In vivo Mutagenesis and Evolution), a plasmid-based orthogonal DNA replication system for continuous directed evolution in Escherichia coli. PRIME harnesses protein-primed DNA replication to establish an autonomous replicon that operates independently of the host genome. Coupling this system to an error-prone DNA polymerase enables targeted diversification of constructs encoded on the orthogonal plasmid while preserving genomic integrity. papers.title: Reassessing the contribution of the histone H3 tail to KRAB-DNMT3L-mediated epigenetic silencing

papers.title: Coupling a developmental promoter to CRISPR interference for Wnt pathway regulation in human pluripotent stem cells
papers.summary: While directed differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells commonly relies on the timed delivery of extracellular factors, these uniform treatments often yield heterogeneous responses across cell populations. Linking intracellular gene regulation directly to an emerging developmental state offers a complementary strategy to coordinate these differentiation signals from within the cell. papers.title: Gene expression noise is reduced in communicating synthetic cell populations
papers.summary: A major goal in bottom-up synthetic biology is the construction of multicellular synthetic systems capable of coordinated and robust collective behaviours. However, robustness is often limited by noise and variability arising from increased molecular complexity. Whilst communication has been implemented in synthetic multi-cellular systems, the ability for communication to suppress cell free gene expression variability in populations of synthetic cells remain unexplored. To address this, we encapsulated the Lux and Las quorum sensing gene circuits in lipid vesicles under cell-free conditions to test the effect of communication on reducing cell-free gene expression variability across the population. papers.title: Boolean Logic-responsive FRET Biosensors via Genetically Encoded Autonomous Compilation
papers.summary: Forster resonance energy transfer (FRET) is commonly used to monitor protein-protein interactions in situ. The high spatiotemporal resolution and facile implementation inside complex molecular environments have spearheaded FRET's widespread adoption in biosensing. Despite these advantages, current FRET biosensors are largely restricted to the detection of the presence/absence of individual inputs and are thus unable to sense several multiplexable inputs simultaneously within complex milieu of biological environments. In this work, we introduce a generalizable strategy to construct genetically encoded protein-based FRET biosensors capable of recognizing multiple inputs following Boolean logic-type (YES/OR/AND) operations. These topologically specified FRET sensors powerfully expand the input capacity in sensing protein-protein interactions while providing a user-programmable platform for monitoring heterogeneous biological activities both in vitro and in living cells.

papers.summary: Glucoamylase is essential for industrial starch saccharification, but the limited thermostability and near-neutral pH tolerance of fungal glucoamylases necessitate cooling and acidification of liquefied starch. papers.title: Constructing Virtual Viruses in A Spatial Minimal Cell
papers.summary: Viral development links gene expression and genome replication to particle formation within a cell. Here we construct virtual viruses in a JCVI-syn3A-based spatial minimal cell. For mycoplasma virus P1, molecular events connect expression and replication to coarse-grained packaging, followed by a spatial reconstruction of membrane opening and particle release. Individual finite-size particles coexist, move across the boundary and undergo partial crossings and returns before complete exit. In contrast, Acholeplasma phage MV-L1 (L1) expresses its genes and accumulates genomes as the host continues to grow and develops a constricted shape. The coexistence of viral activity and continued host growth is qualitatively consistent with the non-lytic biology of group 1 acholeplasmaviruses. These reconstructions extend the virtual cell to the viruses that develop within it, linking molecular activity, particle behavior and host growth.

papers.summary: Synthetic biologists aim for standardization and simplicity in order to ensure reproducibility and reliability. papers.summary: Synthetic biology enables the rational reprogramming of microorganisms into living therapeutics and agents for bioremediation. papers.summary: Engineered living materials (ELMs) offer a promising route to biologically manufactured materials for healthcare, construction and manufacturing. papers.summary: Abstract We developed CUT&ID to simultaneously profile the native genomics and proteomics associations of any endogenous target, in a single workflow with no need for transgenesis. Background: Diseases related to human papillomavirus (HPV) include warts, lesions, and cancers. ICL is idiopathic CD4 T cell lymphocytopenia. People with this rare disease get more HPV-related diseases than other people do. The diseases are more severe and harder to treat in people with ICL. Researchers want to see if the vaccine GARDASIL 9 can help people with ICL. Objective: To study the effects of the vaccine GARDASIL 9 in people with ICL. Eligibility: Adults ages 18-65 with ICL Healthy volunteers the same age Design: Participants will be screened with a physical exam, medical history, and blood and pregnancy tests. Participants will have a baseline visit with: * Physical exam * Medical history * Oral rinse collection. Participants will gargle a small amount of a saline solution, then spit it into a cup. * Apheresis. Blood will be removed through a needle in an arm. A machine will separate the blood and keep some parts for research. The rest will be returned to the participant through a needle in the other arm. * Examination for HP

pipeline.title: A Clinical Study of Intismeran Autogene (V940) and BCG in People With Bladder Cancer (V940-011/INTerpath-011)
pipeline.content: [PHASE2] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC | 适应症: Urinary Bladder Neoplasms, Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Neoplasms, Carcinoma in Situ. Researchers are looking for new ways to treat people with high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (HR NMIBC). NMIBC is cancer in the tissue that lines the inside of the bladder but has not spread to the bladder muscle or outside of the bladder. High-risk means NMIBC may have a high chance of getting worse or coming back after treatment. HR NMIBC can also include carcinoma in situ (CIS). CIS is bladder cancer that appears flat and is only in the inner layer (surface) of the bladder. CIS is not raised and is not growing toward the center of the bladder. The standard treatment for HR NMIBC is a procedure to remove the tumor called transurethral resection of the bladder tumor (TURBT) followed by Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG). Standard treatment is something that is considered the first line of treatment for a condition. BCG is an immunotherapy, which is a treatment that helps the immune system fight cancer.
